name: MiFID II — Markets in Financial Instruments Directive

articles.title: Scope
articles.requirement: Applies to investment firms, market operators, data reporting services providers, and third-country firms providing investment services within the Union.

articles.title: Requirement for authorisation
articles.requirement: Investment firms must be authorised by the competent authority of their home Member State before providing investment services or performing investment activities.

articles.title: Conditions for authorisation
articles.requirement: Competent authorities shall grant authorisation only if satisfied that the applicant meets requirements relating to initial capital, management, organisation, shareholders, and programme of operations.

articles.title: Management body
articles.requirement: Members of the management body must be of sufficiently good repute and possess sufficient knowledge, skills, and experience. The management body must define and oversee the firm's strategy and risk framework.

articles.title: Shareholders and members with qualifying holdings
articles.requirement: Competent authorities must be informed of any natural or legal person proposing to acquire a qualifying holding, and must assess the suitability of the proposed acquirer.

articles.title: Organisational requirements
articles.requirement: Investment firms must have sound governance arrangements including clear organisational structure, effective risk management, adequate internal control mechanisms, and appropriate remuneration policies.

articles.title: Algorithmic trading
articles.requirement: Investment firms engaged in algorithmic trading must have effective systems and risk controls, notify competent authorities, and ensure algorithms do not contribute to disorderly markets.

articles.title: Trading process and finalisation of transactions in MTFs and OTFs
articles.requirement: Operators of MTFs and OTFs must establish transparent and non-discretionary rules for fair and orderly trading, objective criteria for efficient execution of orders, and access requirements.

articles.title: Obligation to make public regular reports
articles.requirement: Market operators must make public information on the quality of execution of transactions on their venues, including details about speed, likelihood of execution, and costs.

articles.title: Obligation to trade on regulated markets, MTFs, or OTFs
articles.requirement: Investment firms must ensure trades in shares admitted to trading on a regulated market take place on a regulated market, MTF, systematic internaliser, or equivalent third-country venue.

articles.title: General principles and information to clients
articles.requirement: Investment firms must act honestly, fairly, and professionally in the best interest of clients. All information to clients must be fair, clear, and not misleading.

articles.title: Assessment of suitability and appropriateness
articles.requirement: When providing investment advice or portfolio management, firms must obtain information about the client's knowledge, experience, financial situation, and investment objectives to assess suitability.

articles.title: Provision of services through another investment firm
articles.requirement: Where an investment firm receives instructions through another firm, the receiving firm may rely on client information transmitted, but responsibility for suitability remains allocated per agreement.

articles.title: Obligation to execute orders on terms most favourable to the client
articles.requirement: Investment firms must take all sufficient steps to obtain the best possible result for clients (best execution) taking into account price, costs, speed, likelihood of execution, settlement size, and nature of the order.

articles.title: Client order handling rules
articles.requirement: Investment firms must implement procedures for prompt, fair, and expeditious execution of client orders relative to other client orders and the firm's own-account trading interests.

articles.title: Obligations of firms employing tied agents
articles.requirement: Investment firms using tied agents remain fully and unconditionally responsible for the agents' acts and must ensure they disclose the capacity in which they act.

articles.title: Transactions with eligible counterparties
articles.requirement: Investment firms may enter into transactions with eligible counterparties without being bound by certain conduct of business or best execution obligations, provided the counterparty agrees.

articles.title: Monitoring of compliance with MTF and OTF rules
articles.requirement: Investment firms and market operators operating MTFs or OTFs must monitor compliance with their rules, report breaches, and notify competent authorities of significant rule violations.

articles.title: Direct electronic access
articles.requirement: Investment firms providing direct electronic access to trading venues must have systems and controls to ensure proper assessment of client suitability and prevent market disorder.

articles.title: General clearing member services
articles.requirement: Investment firms acting as general clearing members must have effective systems and controls to ensure clearing services are applied only to suitable persons meeting clear criteria.

articles.title: Non-discriminatory access to clearing and benchmarks
articles.requirement: CCPs must accept to clear financial instruments on a non-discriminatory and transparent basis, including those traded on different venues.

articles.title: SME growth markets
articles.requirement: MTF operators may apply to have the MTF registered as an SME growth market, provided it meets requirements for issuer admission and ongoing disclosure tailored to SMEs.

articles.title: Pre-trade transparency for MTFs and OTFs — equity
articles.requirement: Market operators and investment firms operating MTFs must make public current bid and offer prices and depth of trading interest for equity instruments.

articles.title: Resilience, circuit breakers, and electronic trading
articles.requirement: Regulated markets must have effective systems, procedures, and arrangements to ensure orderly trading, including resilience of trading systems and circuit breaker mechanisms.

articles.title: Admission of financial instruments to trading
articles.requirement: Regulated markets must have clear, transparent, and non-discriminatory rules for the admission of financial instruments to trading.

articles.title: Suspension and removal of instruments from trading
articles.requirement: Competent authorities may require suspension or removal of a financial instrument from trading where the instrument no longer complies with rules or there is a threat to investor protection or market integrity.

articles.title: Position reporting by categories of position holders
articles.requirement: Member States shall ensure that investment firms and market operators operating a trading venue which trade commodity derivatives report to the competent authority a breakdown of positions held by all persons.

articles.title: Position reporting by categories of position holders
articles.requirement: Investment firms trading in commodity derivatives must report to the competent authority daily details of their own and their clients' positions, classified by category of position holder.

articles.title: Transaction reporting
articles.requirement: Investment firms must report to the competent authority complete and accurate details of executed transactions as quickly as possible and no later than the close of the following working day.

articles.title: Data reporting services
articles.requirement: Data reporting services providers (ARMs, APAs, CTPs) must be authorised and must comply with organisational requirements ensuring accurate, complete, and timely data publication.

articles.title: Supervisory powers
articles.requirement: Competent authorities must have all supervisory and investigatory powers necessary, including the power to access documents, require information, carry out inspections, and suspend marketing or trading.

articles.title: Sanctions
articles.requirement: Member States must provide for effective, proportionate, and dissuasive administrative sanctions and measures for breaches, including fines up to EUR 5M for natural persons and EUR 5M or 10% of turnover for legal persons.

articles.title: Cooperation between competent authorities
articles.requirement: Competent authorities of different Member States must cooperate and exchange information for supervisory purposes, including information about breaches and suspicious activities.

articles.title: Exchange of information with ESMA
articles.requirement: Competent authorities must provide ESMA with information necessary for the performance of its duties, including information on authorisations, supervisory activities, and enforcement.

articles.title: Professional secrecy
articles.requirement: All persons working for competent authorities are bound by professional secrecy, with information received used only for the purposes of supervisory duties.
